markdown:
## Bottom line
**Suggests InSitu (97%)** · Confident · Careful review
Single-class conformal set, but the second model disagrees and the image is blurred.

## Confidence
| Signal | Value | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| Top probabilities | InSitu 97%, Invasive 3% | Strongly favors InSitu |
| Conformal set | {InSitu} at 90% | Single class |
| Reliability / OOD | 0.99 / 96th percentile | Reliable; OOD percentile high |
| Second-model (MUSK) agreement | No | Different top class |
| Similar cases | 3 of 5 InSitu | Nearest two Benign |

## Tissue evidence
- **Atypical cells confined within ducts** (region 5) · ↓ invasive · Highest-scoring concept here; associated with non-invasive disease. · Weak
- **Benign fibrous stroma or fat** (regions 7, 11) · ↓ invasive · Above-typical score; linked to lower invasive likelihood. · Validated
- **Marked nuclear pleomorphism** (region 7) · ↑ invasive · Below-typical score; slightly lowers invasive term. · Validated
- **Tumor infiltrating stroma** (region 7) · ↑ invasive · Typical score; concept model leans slightly away from invasive. · Validated

## Trust check
- **Heatmap**: Removing the top 3 regions drops the invasive logit 0.54 more than random (CI 0.47–0.60): faithful.
- **Concepts**: Deletion CI (−0.005 to 0.007) includes 0, so not shown to reflect the classifier; lymphocytes (8/20) and normal lobules (0/20) are Unreliable here.

## Could be wrong if
- Blur (severity 3) distorts detail, and the MUSK model picks a different top class.
- Both nearest reference cases are Benign; only 3 of 5 neighbors match InSitu.

## Check on the slide
1. **9** Highest per-region invasive probability (55%); look for stromal invasion.
2. **5** Confirm atypical cells stay inside intact ducts.
3. **3, 7, 11** Lateral margin column: confirm tumor-at-margin call [F7]; check invasion in region 7.
